title: Medicare telehealth use and state context

associations.method: Unweighted Pearson correlation across states and DC; descriptive only
associations.limitation: The Pearson correlations are unadjusted ecological associations. The separate adjustedModel includes broadband and income only; neither analysis supports individual-level or causal interpretation.

coefficients.label: Intercept
coefficients.units: percentage points at zero broadband and zero income; outside the observed range

coefficients.label: Broadband subscription, per 1 percentage point
coefficients.units: telehealth percentage points per 1 percentage-point higher broadband subscription

coefficients.label: Median household income, per $10,000
coefficients.units: telehealth percentage points per $10,000 higher median household income

adjustedModel.confidenceInterval: Approximate 95% normal interval: coefficient +/- 1.959964 × HC3 SE; not a t interval
notes: States and DC receive equal weight; ACS is matched only to 2024 CMS annual records.
Both covariates enter simultaneously. Broadband is measured in percentage points and income in $10,000 units.
HC3 addresses heteroskedasticity, not spatial dependence, confounding, or ACS measurement error.
This is an ecological observational association; state household context is not individual beneficiary exposure.
Linear functional form, influential-state sensitivity, spatial residuals, and alternative specifications have not been evaluated.
R-squared describes fit in these 51 observations; it is not a measure of predictive performance. No forecasts or individual predictions are generated.

checksPassed: CMS rates independently recalculated from counts
No negative Census sentinel values used as numeric estimates

definitions.population: CMS: Medicare Part B fee-for-service service users. ACS: all households in each state and DC, not Medicare beneficiaries.
definitions.telehealthPct: 100 × unique beneficiaries receiving at least one telehealth service / unique beneficiaries receiving at least one telehealth-eligible service. Includes audio-only telehealth. Published fraction multiplied by 100.
definitions.eligibleUsers: Unique beneficiaries receiving a telehealth-eligible service in that reporting period, including in-person services. This is the rate denominator.
definitions.partBEnrollment: Published person-year/person-quarter Part B FFS enrollment measure; not used as the telehealth rate denominator.
definitions.annual: CMS quarter=Overall records count unique users across the year. Annual counts/rates are not sums or means of quarterly values.
definitions.quarterly: Separate quarterly reporting periods; a beneficiary can appear in more than one quarter.
definitions.broadbandPct: 2024 ACS 1-year B28002_004E / B28002_001E × 100: households with broadband of any type, including cellular-only subscriptions, divided by all households. Subscription is not equivalent to speed, reliability, or digital literacy.
definitions.medianIncome: 2024 ACS 1-year B19013_001E; median household income in 2024 inflation-adjusted US dollars.
definitions.acsVariableNames: Table-based fields B28002_E004, B28002_E001, B19013_E001 correspond to API fields B28002_004E, B28002_001E, B19013_001E.
definitions.uncertainty: CMS administrative aggregates have no survey sampling confidence interval supplied. ACS margins of error use the published 90% confidence level.
definitions.broadbandMoe90: Derived approximate 90% margin of error, percentage points: 100 × sqrt(MOE_numerator² − p² × MOE_denominator²) / denominator. Use plus if the radicand is negative. Source: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/statistical_testing/2024_Instructions_for_Stat_Testing_ACS.pdf
definitions.national: CMS published National aggregate is retained as supplied; it is not reconstructed by summing the 50 states and DC and can include other geographic categories.
definitions.missing: Blank/suppressed/non-numeric CMS values and negative ACS sentinel values map to null, never zero. All selected source values in this snapshot are available.
definitions.yearMatching: ACS is matched only to 2024 CMS annual records. No ACS values are extrapolated to other years.

limitations: State geography follows beneficiary mailing address. The mapped population is Medicare Part B FFS, not the entire US population.
CMS and ACS describe different populations; state-level context does not identify individual broadband access or income.
Changes in enrollment, reimbursement policy, coding and service eligibility can affect observed trends.
The snapshot uses a later CMS release than the original milestone documentation; historical values may have been revised.
Suppression rules apply to the underlying CMS release. No suppressed values are reconstructed.
The adjusted state regression includes broadband and income only; unmeasured confounding and ecological bias remain. No prediction or causal model is reported.
